question: Should experimental Claws be allowed to register arbitrary manifest-provided stdio commands and reuse exact global MCP names, or must both actions pass an explicit host broker/authorization contract?
rationale: This defines the permanent execution and cross-role ownership boundary for a persisted OpenClaw MCP configuration surface; it cannot be safely inferred from local shape validation or contributor intent.

options.title: Require brokered commands and authorized sharing
options.body: Require a host-approved command/broker path and an explicit host authorization record before a Claw can create or reuse a global MCP declaration.

options.title: Accept unrestricted experimental ownership
options.body: Keep arbitrary manifest commands and exact global reuse under the experimental flag, explicitly accepting the host-level execution and cross-role ownership risk.

options.title: Defer MCP lifecycle ownership
options.body: Pause this PR's MCP mutation slice until the RFC or a narrower core capability defines the authorization contract.

recommendation.title: Require brokered commands and authorized sharing
recommendation.body: Require a host-approved command/broker path and an explicit host authorization record before a Claw can create or reuse a global MCP declaration.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned to this PR and has already reviewed the relevant config, lifecycle, and recovery boundaries.
